statement: These committed receipts were produced under an earlier ruleset. They are not receipts of the current transition protocol and must not be read as one.
how_these_differ: Their timestamps are read from a host clock, so the same transition yields different content on every run.
They are written by test modules and validation scripts rather than appended to a ledger.
They carry no hb_reference, no previous_receipt_sha256 and no chain position, so they cannot be replayed or reconstructed as a chain.
Five are written at module import, so collecting the test file rewrites the committed file.
observable_consequence: A repository sweep leaves these files modified with no source change, because the suite rewrote them with the run's own clock. The churn is the finding, not a defect introduced by whatever change was being tested.
clock_source: llm_adapter/retrieval_evidence.py::evidence_pointer defaults retrieved_at to utc_now_iso(), which reads datetime.now(timezone.utc)

excluded_from_this_register.reason: Preflight mutation-safety manifests are authored deliberately per change set and are not produced by a run.

remediation_not_performed_here: Stop test modules writing committed receipts; a run's output belongs outside the committed tree.
Supply retrieved_at from the heartbeat rather than defaulting it to a host clock, so a receipt's content does not depend on when it was produced.
Decide per receipt whether it is a ledger transition, which would place it on the chain, or a validation artifact, which should not be committed as a receipt at all.
